mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the GLK 220 CDI costs £2,400-£3,400 supply-only; a rebuilt OM651 engine for the GLK 250 CDI costs £2,800-£3,700 supply-only. Fitting adds £700-£1,300 depending on complexity.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. If ignored, it can lead to misfires, cam/crank correlation codes, and catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI engine (OM651) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 is fundamentally reliable - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch from approximately 120,000 km, early Delphi injector failures, EGR clogging, and water pump leaks. All are manageable with the right maintenance schedule and proactive attention.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLK 220 CDI and 250 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000+ miles before major work is needed. With timely timing chain service and regular maintenance, these engines demonstrate exceptional longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLK is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £2,400-£3,700 - comparable to or less than replacing a £4,000-£12,000 vehicle, especially when factoring in the cost of finding a comparable replacement SUV.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM651 requires approximately 6.5 litres with filter.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLK Class 220 CDI/250 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLK 220 CDI and 250 CDI represented the core of the X204 diesel lineup from launch in 2008 through to production end in 2015. Powered by the OM651 2.1-litre twin-turbo four-cylinder diesel - available in 170hp and 204hp outputs - these variants accounted for the vast majority of UK GLK sales and continue to drive the highest volume of engine replacement enquiries.

items.title: 2.1L Twin-Turbo Diesel (2008-2015)
items.commonFailure: Timing chain stretch and guide wear - the OM651's single most critical failure point. The rear-mounted timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. If it stretches beyond tolerance or a guide fails, the consequences range from misfires to catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth. Typical failure mileage: 75,000-120,000 miles (120,000-200,000 km).
items.cta: -> Get quotes for OM651.911 Mercedes GLK 220 CDI engine replacement

items.title: 2.1L Twin-Turbo Diesel (2009-2015)
items.commonFailure: Secondary turbo wastegate actuator failure - the twin-turbo setup adds complexity, with the secondary turbo actuator prone to sticking due to carbon buildup. Timing chain stretch and guide wear also affect higher-output variants. Injector seat carbon leakage causing rough idle is another documented issue. Typical failure mileage: 60,000-100,000 miles.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLK Class 220 CDI/250 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM651 twin-turbo diesel is the backbone of the GLK diesel range - fundamentally reliable and capable of 200,000-300,000 km with proper maintenance. However, it has well-documented weak points that drive replacement enquiries. The single most critical failure is timing chain stretch from approximately 120,000 km (75,000 miles), followed by EGR cooler cracking, turbo actuator issues, and injector failures. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.group: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Wear
problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Wear - The Most Critical GLK Diesel Failure
problems.rootCause: The OM651's timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. A hydraulic tensioner loses pressure prematurely, allowing chain stretch and guide wear. A distinctive rattling noise on cold starts is the classic warning sign. If ignored, the chain can snap or jump a tooth, causing catastrophic valve and piston collision.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught immediately when rattle first appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioner, rails; no engine removal required
repairOptions.longevity: If chain rattle is present but no fault codes

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded timing chain kit, new injectors, and upgraded EGR components fitted as standard
repairOptions.longevity: If chain has jumped causing valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2008-2015 GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI 4MATIC is worth approximately £4,000-£12,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLK 220/250 CDI sits in the £4,000-£12,000 band - replacement cost is typically justified for well-maintained examples, though owners of higher-mileage or lower-value examples should carefully evaluate repair costs against vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If your GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The OM651's timing chain is accessible with the engine in situ for tensioner and chain replacement, though guides typically require more extensive work. Specialist pricing of £950-£1,500 for a full chain kit is significantly lower than dealer rates. However, if the engine has already suffered timing jump or oil pressure loss, a minor repair is a financial risk. We recommend a fully rebuilt OM651 unit, which includes the upgraded tensioner as standard, new injectors, and EGR components - restoring long-term reliability.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM651 Mercedes GLK 220 CDI/250 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: OM651 EGR Cooler Cracking - Coolant Loss and Overheating Risk
problems.rootCause: The shared aluminum EGR cooler (OEM A6511400509) in all OM651-powered GLK 220/250 CDI variants cracks due to thermal cycling stress. This allows coolant to enter the exhaust system or escape externally, leading to coolant loss, overheating, and potential engine damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler unit, coolant flush, gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before overheating damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded stainless-steel EGR cooler and bypass valves
repairOptions.longevity: If coolant loss has caused cylinder head or bottom-end damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical GLK 220/250 CDI is worth £4,000-£12,000.
problems.recommendation: The EGR cooler is a known weak point on all OM651-powered GLK diesels. If you notice coolant loss without an obvious external leak, or if the vehicle runs hotter than normal, have the EGR cooler inspected immediately. Specialist EGR cooler replacement at £500-£750 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. Some specialists offer stainless-steel retrofits with integrated bypass valves, eliminating the risk of repeat failure.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM651 Mercedes GLK 220 CDI/250 CDI engine quotes

problems.h4: OM651 Turbocharger & Injector Failures - Power Loss and Limp Mode
problems.rootCause: Short urban trips and delayed servicing cause carbon accumulation in the EGR system and turbo vanes. The secondary turbo wastegate actuator is particularly prone to sticking. Early Delphi piezo injectors are also prone to failure, causing rough idle, limp mode, and rail pressure errors.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Injector cleaning or single injector replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Ultrasonic cleaning of injectors, leak-off test; or replace faulty injector

repairOptions.longevity: If actuator is sticking but turbo bearings intact

repairOptions.tier: Major - Full turbocharger replacement (secondary or both)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty turbo(s), oil feed lines, gaskets
Complete engine swap with new turbos, upgraded injectors, and EGR components
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo debris has circulated or multiple injectors have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - a typical GLK 220/250 CDI is worth £4,000-£12,000.
problems.recommendation: If you experience rough idle, limp mode, or power loss on your GLK 220 CDI or 250 CDI, have a diagnostic scan performed immediately. Replacing a single faulty injector at a specialist (£250-£450) is cost-effective. However, if multiple injectors are failing, replacing all four with the later magnetic-type units is the smarter long-term investment - early Delphi piezo injectors are prone to repeat failure. For turbo actuator issues, replacement at £350-£550 is significantly cheaper than a full turbocharger replacement.
